sentences.zh: 我想他已经有，我不知道，好久没写过非脱欧的故事了，这就是他的生活。

sentences.en: It is a completely all-consuming story because there's always a political crisis either brewing or actually happening in Britain at the moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个完全吞噬一切的故事，因为目前英国总是有政治危机在酝酿或正在发生。

sentences.en: So remind me how this all began.
sentences.zh: 所以提醒我这一切是怎么开始的。

sentences.en: What got Britain to this point?
sentences.zh: 是什么让英国走到了这一步？

sentences.en: Yes, thinking back, it was the 23rd of June in 2016 and...
sentences.zh: 是的，回想起来，那是2016年6月23日，而且……

sentences.en: Good evening and welcome at the end of this momentous day when each one of us has had the chance to say what kind of country we want to live in.
sentences.zh: 晚上好，欢迎来到这个重大的日子结束之际，在这个日子里，我们每个人都有机会表达我们想生活在什么样的国家。

sentences.en: Britons were voting on whether to leave the European Union.
sentences.zh: 英国人在投票决定是否留在欧盟。

sentences.en: At 10 o'clock, the polling stations close after weeks, months, years of argument.
sentences.zh: 在10点钟，经过几个星期、几个月、几年的争论后，投票站关闭了。

sentences.en: And we'll have the answer to the question that's haunted British politics for so long.
sentences.zh: 我们将得到那个长期困扰英国政治的问题的答案。

sentences.en: Do we want to be in or out of the EU?
sentences.zh: 我们是想留在欧盟内部还是退出？

sentences.en: What I remember of that day was I came in a little late and completely by coincidence, as I was walking to the Bureau, I happened to bump into somebody
sentences.zh: 我对那一天的记忆是我稍微晚了一点到办公室，完全出于巧合，当我走向分社时，我碰巧遇到了一个人

sentences.en: who was actually canvassing in the street and it was an advisor to David Cameron, who was then the Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 他当时正在街上拉票，那是时任首相大卫·卡梅伦的一位顾问。

sentences.en: And we had a conversation and he assured me that Remain was going to win the referendum.
sentences.zh: 我们交谈了一番，他向我保证留欧派将在公投中获胜。

sentences.en: So I came into the office pretty relaxed about what I thought was going to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以我来到办公室时，对即将发生的事情感到相当轻松。

sentences.en: I hereby give notice that I have certified the following.
sentences.zh: 我在此通知，我已证实了以下内容。

sentences.en: The total number of ballot papers counted was...
sentences.zh: 清点的选票总数是……

sentences.en: But then the results started coming in.
sentences.zh: 但随后结果开始出炉。

sentences.en: The total number of votes cast in favour of Leave was 63,598.
sentences.zh: 投赞成脱欧的选票总数为63,598张。

sentences.en: It shows the Leave campaign just a little bit behind Remain, not nearly as much behind as all the experts had been saying we should expect from Newcastle.
sentences.zh: 这表明脱欧阵营仅稍微落后于留欧阵营，远没有像所有专家所说的那样，我们应该预料到纽卡斯尔会落后那么多。

sentences.en: It very soon became clear that things were not going according to plan for Downing Street.
sentences.zh: 很快就很明显，事情并没有按唐宁街的计划进行。

sentences.en: The total number of votes cast in favour of Leave was 82,000.
sentences.zh: 投赞成脱欧的选票总数为82,000张。

sentences.en: To say these results are interesting is an understatement.
sentences.zh: 要说这些结果很有趣，那真是保守的说法。

sentences.en: As the results went on through the night, it became clearer and clearer that actually Britain had voted to leave the European Union.
sentences.zh: 随着夜间结果的公布，越来越清楚的是，实际上英国已经投票决定离开欧盟。

sentences.en: The British people have spoken and the answer is we're out.
sentences.zh: 英国人民已经发声，答案是我们出局了。

sentences.en: Against almost everybody's expectations.
sentences.zh: 违背了几乎所有人的预期。

sentences.en: And this is a vote that has huge consequences, not just for our country, but also implications for a whole continent.
sentences.zh: 这是一场具有巨大后果的投票，不仅对我们的国家，而且对整个欧洲大陆都有深远的影响。

sentences.en: And it unleashes a period of huge uncertainty, maybe huge opportunity, but also maybe huge risks too.
sentences.zh: 它释放了一个充满巨大不确定性的时期，也许有巨大的机遇，但也可能伴随着巨大的风险。

sentences.en: And what was the context for this referendum?
sentences.zh: 这次公投的背景是什么？

sentences.en: How did this come to be?
sentences.zh: 这究竟是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Well, you have to look back to the way that the European Union was founded.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你必须回溯欧盟创立的方式。

sentences.en: It was founded by six countries after the Second World War and Britain stayed out of it for a long time.
sentences.zh: 它是由六个国家在二战后创立的，英国很长一段时间都没有加入。

sentences.en: It was never really emotionally committed to this idea of European integration in the way that perhaps the French and the Germans and the Dutch, the Italians were.
sentences.zh: 它从未真正从情感上投入到这种欧洲一体化的理念中，就像法国、德国、荷兰和意大利那样。

sentences.en: And Britain only really joined it because in 1973, it felt it was falling behind continental Europe.
sentences.zh: 英国加入它其实只是因为在1973年，它觉得自己在落后于欧洲大陆。

sentences.en: It joined it really much more for transactional reasons.
sentences.zh: 它加入更多是出于交易性的原因。

sentences.en: And therefore, our whole idea of European integration never really had that same force and that same salience in British life.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们对欧洲一体化的整体理念在英国生活中从未真正具有那种相同的力量和重要性。

sentences.en: So the context of the referendum was that many of the Conservatives have become increasingly unhappy with the direction of the European Union.
sentences.zh: 所以公投的背景是，许多保守党人对欧盟的发展方向越来越不满。

sentences.en: And we find ourselves today part of a political union.
sentences.zh: 我们今天发现自己是一个政治联盟的一部分。

sentences.en: We find most of our laws being made somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 我们发现我们的大多数法律都是在别处制定的。

sentences.en: We find it's all rather expensive.
sentences.zh: 我们发现这一切相当昂贵。

sentences.en: And we have open-door immigration.
sentences.zh: 而且我们实行门户开放的移民政策。

sentences.en: They felt that it was becoming much more intrusive into British life.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得欧盟对英国生活干涉得越来越多了。

sentences.en: And they felt that this surrender of sovereignty was becoming more and more intrusive and more and more unbearable for them.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得这种主权的让渡变得越来越具有侵略性，对他们来说也越来越难以忍受。

sentences.en: And it became more and more acute in the Conservative Party, which was also under pressure from some populist forces on the right.
sentences.zh: 这种情绪在保守党内部变得越来越尖锐，保守党当时也承受着来自右翼一些民粹主义力量的压力。

sentences.en: In fact, US strategists are saying that what's happening is that Britain is looking inwards.
sentences.zh: 事实上，美国策略师表示，发生的事情是英国正在向内看。

sentences.en: Anti-immigration, looking at whether it's going to pull out of the European Union, looking at all these different areas.
sentences.zh: 反移民，考虑是否要退出欧盟，审视所有这些不同的领域。

sentences.en: Britain seems to be retrenching from a global position.
sentences.zh: 英国似乎在从全球立场收缩。

sentences.en: David Cameron, who leads the centre-right Conservative Party, closest traditionally to the Republicans in the United States, he promised to hold the referendum
sentences.zh: 领导中右翼保守党（传统上最接近美国共和党）的大卫·卡梅伦承诺，如果他再次当选

sentences.en: if he was going to be re-elected.
sentences.zh: 他将举行公投。

sentences.en: He was facing an election in 2015.
sentences.zh: 他面临着2015年的选举。

sentences.en: He, I think, to probably his surprise, won a clear majority in that election.
sentences.zh: 我想，可能出乎他自己的意料，他在那次选举中赢得了绝对多数。

sentences.en: It is time for the British people to have their say.
sentences.zh: 是时候让英国人民发表意见了。

sentences.en: It is time for us to settle this question about Britain and Europe.
sentences.zh: 是时候让我们解决关于英国和欧洲的这个问题了。

sentences.en: Therefore, had to go through with this pledge to hold the referendum on whether or not Britain was going to stay or leave the European Union.
sentences.zh: 因此，他不得不兑现举行关于英国是否留在欧盟的公投的承诺。

sentences.en: It will be an in-out referendum.
sentences.zh: 这将是一场留欧与退欧的公投。

sentences.en: And what exactly was fueling this pressure by Conservatives in his party?
sentences.zh: 究竟是什么在助长他党内保守派的这种压力？

sentences.en: Well, one of the key elements of the European Union is that you can go and live anywhere in the European Union.
sentences.zh: 嗯，欧盟的关键要素之一就是你可以去欧盟的任何地方生活。

sentences.en: So one of the big issues here became migration.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的一个大问题成了移民。

sentences.en: And that really arose out of the enlargement of the European Union in 2004, when it took in 10 mainly ex-communist countries.
sentences.zh: 这实际上源于2004年欧盟的扩大，当时它接纳了10个主要是前共产主义国家。

sentences.en: Millions of new migrants could set foot on European soil next year unless steps are taken immediately.
sentences.zh: 除非立即采取措施，否则明年将有数百万新移民踏上欧洲土地。

sentences.en: And Britain became one of only three countries which didn't restrict its labour market to all these migrants.
sentences.zh: 英国成为仅有的三个不对所有这些移民开放劳动力市场的国家之一。

sentences.en: In the UK town of Boston, the number of Poles, Lithuanians and Latvians has increased sixfold in 10 years.
sentences.zh: 在英国小镇波士顿，波兰人、立陶宛人和拉脱维亚人的数量在10年内增加了六倍。

sentences.en: At the time, it thought some migration would be good for the economy, which it probably was, but it's stored up trouble for the future.
sentences.zh: 当时，人们认为一些移民对经济会有好处，可能确实如此，但也为未来埋下了隐患。

sentences.en: They've arrived here under European Union freedom of movement rules in search of work.
sentences.zh: 他们根据欧盟的人员自由流动规则来到这里寻找工作。

sentences.en: But some locals feel overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 但一些当地人感到不堪重负。

sentences.en: It's these Roma gypsies that are coming.
sentences.zh: 是这些罗姆吉普赛人来了。

sentences.en: I think they could be a problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们可能会是个问题。

sentences.en: Britain had only expected tens of thousands of people to come and in the end, around about a million people came.
sentences.zh: 英国原本只预计会有几万人到来，但最终大约有一百万人到来。

sentences.en: And that, in a sense,
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，

sentences.en: was manageable until the financial crisis when there were big strains on public services and austerity began to bite.
sentences.zh: 这原本还是可控的，直到金融危机爆发，公共服务承受巨大压力，紧缩政策开始显现。

sentences.en: We literally got swamped by vast numbers of people and our public services couldn't...
sentences.zh: 我们简直被大量的人淹没，我们的公共服务无法……

sentences.en: Who contribute to the economy?
sentences.zh: 谁对经济有贡献？

sentences.en: Who pay their taxes?
sentences.zh: 谁在纳税？

sentences.en: Mostly no.
sentences.zh: 大多数没有。

sentences.en: Mostly no.
sentences.zh: 大多数没有。

sentences.en: What do you mean mostly?
sentences.zh: 你说的“大多数”是什么意思？

sentences.en: And as the impact of that was felt, so the issue of migration increased in the public mind in Britain.
sentences.zh: 随着这种影响的显现，移民问题在英国公众心目中的重要性也随之增加。

sentences.en: Well, I think we're getting too many people coming in, definitely.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为涌入的人太多了，肯定的。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of the people now who are unemployed start to feel bitter about other people coming in and getting jobs.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在很多失业的人开始对其他人进来抢工作感到不满。

sentences.en: I know that for a fact.
sentences.zh: 我很清楚这一点。

sentences.en: So by the time we got to 2016,
sentences.zh: 所以到了2016年，

sentences.en: Britain had been in austerity for at least six or seven years since the financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 自金融危机以来，英国至少已经经历了六七年的紧缩。

sentences.en: And I think there's a fear as well that, you know, they say one day
sentences.zh: 而且我认为也有一种恐惧，你知道，他们说总有一天

sentences.en: England won't be English people here.
sentences.zh: 这里将不再有英国人。

sentences.en: It'll be all foreigners.
sentences.zh: 全都是外国人。

sentences.en: So just so I understand, Stephen, hundreds of thousands of migrants from former Soviet bloc countries start coming into Britain, which causes resentment
sentences.zh: 所以我弄明白了吗，斯蒂芬，成千上万来自前苏联集团国家的移民开始涌入英国，这引起了怨恨

sentences.en: and worry over migrants taking jobs and using social services.
sentences.zh: 并担心移民抢走工作和消耗社会福利。

sentences.en: And at the same time, there is a financial crisis, which causes the UK to tighten its belt across the board.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，发生了金融危机，导致英国全面勒紧裤腰带。

sentences.en: So that resentment and that worry about migrants gets amplified and causes major divisions in the country, which feels similar to what has happened in the United States.
sentences.zh: 因此，对移民的这种怨恨和担忧被放大，并在国内造成了严重的分裂，这感觉与美国发生的事情很相似。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Now, Cameron really had wanted to end these divisions and he wanted to get on with his term in office and get this troublesome question of Europe, which has been nagging away
